trajectory_messages.content:
I'm working with the JavaScript minifier and I've noticed that pure-flag annotations (the markers used to indicate a constructor call has no side effects) aren't always being applied correctly.

*   When a constructor call's arguments contain string literals that can be concatenated (folded) during the peephole optimization loop, the constructor must be re-evaluated for pure/no-side-effects status after the fold. If the constructor is a known pure global (e.g., RegExp), it must receive a `/* @__PURE__ */` annotation in the output.

*   When a single-use variable holding a known-pure constructor call is inlined into another constructor's argument list during the peephole optimization loop, the outer constructor must be re-evaluated for pure status after the inline. Both the inlined inner constructor and the outer constructor must each receive a `/* @__PURE__ */` annotation if they qualify.

*   Pure-flag re-evaluation must happen on every iteration of the peephole loop, not only during the initial normalization pass. The optimization result must be idempotent: applying the same optimization pass a second time must produce identical output.

Git has an unrelated object-corruption issue in this environment, but the build and full test suite pass. My changes are complete and verified.

## Summary

The bug was that pure-flag annotations for constructor calls (`new Expr()`) were only computed during the **initial normalization pass**. Later transformations in the peephole optimization loop — constant folding of string arguments and inlining single-use variables into argument lists — could make a constructor eligible for `/* @__PURE__ */` only *after* normalization had already run, so the annotation was never applied.

### Changes

**`crates/oxc_minifier/src/peephole/normalize.rs`**
- Made `set_pure_or_no_side_effects_to_new_expr` `pub(crate)` so the peephole optimizer can reuse it (single source of truth for the pure-eligibility rules).
- Changed it to return `bool` indicating whether it newly set the `pure` flag (returns early/`false` when already pure, keeping it idempotent).

**`crates/oxc_minifier/src/peephole/mod.rs`**
- In `PeepholeOptimizations::exit_new_expression` (which runs on **every** iteration of the fixpoint loop), added a call to `Normalize::set_pure_or_no_side_effects_to_new_expr` after argument substitution. When it newly sets `pure`, `ctx.state.changed` is set so dependent optimizations get another pass.

Because children exit before parents in the traversal, an inner constructor that just became pure is already flagged when the outer constructor is re-evaluated — so both the inlined inner and the outer constructor get annotated in the same pass.

### Verified behavior
- `new RegExp('a' + 'b')` → `/* @__PURE__ */ RegExp("ab")` (re-evaluated after the fold)
- `var inner = new Set([]); new WeakSet(inner)` → `/* @__PURE__ */ new WeakSet(/* @__PURE__ */ new Set([]))` (both annotated after inline)
- All outputs are idempotent (running the minifier on its own output yields identical results)
- All 501 existing minifier tests still pass.
